title: Supporting Singaporeans in Starting and Raising Families
what_it_is: Supporting Singaporeans in Starting and Raising Families

sections.label: Falling fertility and citizen marriages
sections.summary: The passage reports preschool investment, a 2023 total fertility rate of 0.97, and declining citizen marriages in 2023 and over five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We are also investing significantly in schools, especially preschools, so that every child, regardless of background, gets a good start in life." In 2023, my husband and I welcomed our second bundle of joy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But in that same year, our nation's total fertility rate (TFR) fell to 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On the marriage front, there were 24,355 citizen marriages in 2023, which was a decline of 1.7% from the preceding year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to the Population in Brief 2024, the average number of citizen marriages per year in the last five years was 22,800, which is lower than the preceding five years of 24,000.

sections.label: Singles meeting online
sections.summary: A 2021 survey found the proportion of singles who met through online platforms and started dating rose from 7% in 2012 to 29% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to a 2021 National Population and Talent Division survey, the proportion of singles who met through online platforms and started dating grew more than four-fold, from 7% in 2012 to 29% in 2021.

sections.label: HDB priority for first-timer families
sections.summary: Since August 2022, HDB has prioritised more flats for first-timer families, with specified increases for BTO flats in non-mature and mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since August 2022, Housing and Development Board (HDB) has shared with us that more flats have been prioritised for first-timer families: a 15% increase for 3-room BTO flats in non-mature estates; a 10% increase for 4-room and larger BTO flats in non-mature estates; and 95% of 3-room and larger BTO flats in mature estates.

sections.label: Priority for families with children
sections.summary: Since August 2023, first-timer families with a child aged 18 and below, and first-timer married couples aged 40 and below, have received greater priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In cases where the first-timer families have a child aged 18 and below, as well as for first-timer married couples who are aged 40 and below, these families have been receiving greater priority since August 2023.

sections.label: Housing grant amounts
sections.summary: Up to $80,000 for new flats or up to $160,000 for resale flats is available, with higher amounts for lower-income families, in addition to new flat subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With regard to housing grants, up to $80,000 for new flats or up to $160,000 for resale flats with even higher amounts for lower-income families are available and these are in addition to the subsidies applied to new flats.

sections.label: COV concerns and housing loan flexibility
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on further housing plans and asks HDB to review COV measures and allow flexibility on loans or CPF for COV and repayments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On this note, I seek clarification from the Government as to what other plans and policies, in respect of housing for young couples and growing families, could still be in the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I shared during the 2023 Budget Statement's debate about several of my Woodgrove residents, who commented that as young couples with limited savings, they have opted out of resale flats as an option because the Cash Over Valuation (COV) component is often in the high range, in the region of $30,000 to $50,000, which has to be paid out in cash as it cannot be covered by housing loans or Central Provident Fund (CPF).

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Similar feedback continues to be heard today whenever I probe many of my residents who come to see me about appealing to HDB to increase their chances of securing a Sale of Balance flat and why they do not wish to consider purchasing from the open market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, hope that HDB can review the current measures to continue to ease the COV situation that young couples face or allow for more flexibility in allowing housing loans or CPF savings to be used for the payment of such COV component.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Also, would it possible for families to seek a lower and/or deferred housing loan repayment rate from HDB for the first few years of their child's birth?

sections.label: Government-Paid Paternity Leave increase
sections.summary: Government-Paid Paternity Leave is doubled to four weeks for fathers of children born on or after 1 April, with per-parent allocation rising to five weeks from 1 April next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Government-Paid Paternity Leave has been doubled to four weeks and is applicable to the fathers of children born on or after 1 April this year, as well as adoptive fathers where the eligibility date of application to adopt a child is on or after 1 April 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By default, each parent will be allocated half the entitlement totaling three weeks from 1 April 2025, which is slated to be increased to five weeks per parent from 1 April next year.

sections.label: Baby Bonus release timing
sections.summary: An MP asks the Government to consider releasing the Baby Bonus once the expecting mother clears her first trimester.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Like many parents with young families, I appreciate the Government's enhancement of the Baby Bonus in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, during my interactions with many young parents in Woodgrove, many of them shared their view and their hope that the Government can explore increasing the cash gift component and the release of funds even before the child is born as they have to incur many expenses on things, such as prenatal check-ups, purchase of baby essentials in preparation for the arrival of the baby.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As such, I implore the Government to consider releasing the Baby Bonus once the expecting mother clears her first trimester.

sections.label: HDB and ECDA Anchor Operators
sections.summary: An MP hopes HDB and ECDA review their system to shortlist Anchor Operators early and have them ready when HDB begins key collection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I hope that HDB and the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) can work together to review and improve its current system to shortlist the Anchor Operators that will be serving the estate at the earliest opportunity, even while the BTO project is still under construction and to get the appointed Anchor Operator to set up and be ready to operate once HDB begins its key collection exercise.

sections.label: Kickstart Fund for life milestones
sections.summary: An MP hopes the Kickstart Fund eases financial burdens such as wedding expenses, renovation, prenatal check-ups and confinement costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Without sufficient savings and stable income, many Singaporeans, even when they meet the right partner, will think twice about having a baby immediately after marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope this Kickstart Fund can help Singaporeans when they embark on important life milestones and ease their financial burden, for example, wedding expenses, new home renovation costs, prenatal check-ups and various postpartum confinement expenses, and so on.

sections.label: Paternity leave uptake and mandating
sections.summary: The passage states paternity leave rises to four weeks from April, uptake was low in 2020, and studies suggest mandating such policies could help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore has made strides in improving paternity leave policies with fathers currently entitled to two weeks of paid leave, increasing to four weeks from April this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the uptake remains low with only 44% of eligible fathers fully utilising their leave in 2020, citing workload, stigma and unsupportive workplace cultures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Studies show that mandatory paternity leave increases father involvement by 25%, suggesting that Singapore could benefit from extending and mandating such policies as well.

sections.label: Consolidating childcare leave
sections.summary: The Government can streamline childcare leave for children up to age 12, consider eight uniform days, and allow more leave for parents with two or more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To better caregiving needs, the Government can streamline and consolidate childcare leave for all children up to the age of 12, consider a uniformed eight days of childcare leave across-the-board for children up to 12 and allow higher leave entitlement for parents with two or more children.

sections.label: MSF study on parenting communication
sections.summary: A 2020 MSF study found couples who communicated openly about parenting roles reported stronger relationships and better child outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A 2020 MSF study found that couples who communicated openly about parenting roles reported stronger relationships and better child outcomes.

sections.label: Childcare leave and father protections
sections.summary: It proposes higher childcare leave for parents with two or more children, anti-discrimination protection for fathers taking leave or FWAs, and equitable parental leave sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, higher childcare leave entitlement for parents with two or more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourthly, increased legal protection for fathers who take leave or request FWAs against discrimination based on our existing legislative framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fifthly, encourage couples to share parental leave equitably.

sections.label: Fathers' workshops against patriarchal thinking
sections.summary: Since 2020 workshops and seminars for fathers and young men were co-organised with MSF and Casa Raudha Women Home to eradicate patriarchal thinking and end domestic violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Since 2020, we have also been co-organising with MSF and Casa Raudha Women Home, a series of workshops and seminars for fathers and young men, to eradicate patriarchal thinking and end domestic violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By addressing cultural, workplace and Government policy barriers, Singapore can take the lead in promoting shared parenting and redefining the role of parents.

sections.label: Addressing barriers to shared parenting
sections.summary: It states that addressing cultural, workplace and policy barriers lets Singapore promote shared parenting and redefine fathers' roles, strengthening families and a more equitable society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By addressing cultural workplace and policy barriers, Singapore can lead the way in promoting shared parenting and redefining the roles of fathers, ultimately changing mindsets and empowering fathers to take an active role in parenting, which will strengthen families and contribute to a more equitable society for decades as building blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, let us build a "Singapore Made for Families".

sections.label: Concern over incremental approach to TFR
sections.summary: It says continual policy review is unobjectionable but expresses concern that an incremental approach is being entrenched in tackling the record low TFR of 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There is nothing objectionable to this statement and any government in any country that is doing its job should always continually review and update its policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that we are further entrenching the incremental approach that we are taking in trying to tackle the monumental challenge of our record low TFR of 0.97 that is before us.

sections.label: Eroding FWA normalisation and law request
sections.summary: Citing 2024 survey data on hybrid work and CEO expectations, it expresses concern that FWA normalisation is eroding and reiterates a call to enshrine the right to request FWAs in law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On 30 November 2024, a Straits Times article reported that according to data from Blackbox Research's platform SensingSG, which polls 1,500 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) aged 18 and up every three months, 27% of respondents still enjoy hybrid work arrangements, down seven percentage points year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the same article, KPMG's CEO Outlook, which polled 1,325 CEOs between July and August, highlighted that 83% of bosses expect a full return to office within the next three years, up from 64% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While one can argue that FWAs can take many forms, and indeed there may be jobs where operational demands may mean that work-from-home may not be possible and that other forms of FWAs may be more appropriate, the point remains that I am concerned that the progress we have made in normalising FWAs is quickly eroding away, with employers less likely to even consider other less disruptive forms of FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to reiterate my call made in October 2024 to enshrine into law the right to request for FWAs.

sections.label: IPS survey on Singaporeans' attitudes
sections.summary: An IPS survey shared on 29 January 2024 found seven in 10 Singaporeans aged 21 to 34 feel marriage and children are not necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to an IPS' survey shared at the Singapore Perspectives conference on 29 January 2024, on Singaporeans' attitudes and views toward issues, such as family, well-being and work, seven in 10 of Singaporeans in the youngest group aged 21 to 34 feel it is not necessary to get married and have children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Across all age groups surveyed, the main reasons among this include a career focus, lacking time and energy and being deterred by the high stress and costs of doing so.

sections.label: Reviewing policies and fertility rate
sections.summary: The speaker questions whether the incremental approach has changed the status quo of Singapore's record-low total fertility rate of 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There is nothing objectionable to this statement and any government in any country that is doing its job should always continually review and update its policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that we are further entrenching the incremental approach that we are taking in trying to tackle the monumental challenge of our record-low total fertility rate of 0.97 that is before us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Three years on after the "A Singapore Made for Families 2025" plan was announced back in 2022, have we truly changed the status quo?

sections.label: Job insecurity and caregiving
sections.summary: The speaker says parents should not suffer job insecurity for prioritising caregiving or extending parental leave in their children's early years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Feeling like your job or future career is at risk if one chooses to prioritise caregiving in the early years of parenthood is very real.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A "Singapore Made for Families" should be one where parents should not suffer from job insecurity because they choose to extend parental leave or prioritise caregiving during their children’s formative years.

sections.label: Changing social compact frame
sections.summary: The speaker says the key is changing the frame of the social compact with young Singaporeans to build a Singapore Made for Families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The key lies in how we change the frame of our social compact with young Singaporeans to truly build a "Singapore Made for Families", a society that values parenthood deeply.

sections.label: Championing parenthood social compact
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the frame of the social compact with young Singaporeans can be changed to champion parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: How can we change the frame of our social compact with young Singaporeans to build a "Singapore Made for Families" to one that champions parenthood?

sections.label: Support for the Motion
sections.summary: The speaker states that at this point they support the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Yes, at this point, we do support the Motion.

sections.label: Low TFR called serious problem
sections.summary: Lee Hsien Loong in 2004 called the low TFR a very serious problem, and it hit a new low of 0.97 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: During his first National Day Rally speech in 2004, then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong had already pointed out that the low TFR was, I quote, "a very serious problem for us".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has since hit a new low of 0.97 in 2023.

sections.label: Falling TFR and immigration reliance
sections.summary: Despite policies like Baby Bonus, parental leave and IVF support, TFR kept falling, and the Government largely relied on immigration for the population shortfall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Despite decades of policies, like the Baby Bonus scheme, increased parental leave and financial support for in-vitro fertilisation (IVF), our TFR has continued to fall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the birth rate continues to fall, the Government has largely relied on immigration to make up for the population shortfall.

sections.label: PSP Affordable Homes Scheme
sections.summary: PSP proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme, which reduces BTO flat prices by removing land cost for owner-occupied flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For housing, PSP has proposed the Affordable Homes Scheme, which reduces the price of BTO flats by removing the cost of land for owner-occupied flats.

sections.label: Healthier Mother Cash Gift
sections.summary: PSP proposes a new $3,000 Healthier Mother Cash Gift paid to every mother upon the birth of each child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To help mothers defray this cost, PSP proposes a new $3,000 Healthier Mother Cash Gift, paid to every mother upon the birth of each child.

sections.label: Wage claim for flexi-time workers
sections.summary: PSP proposes letting companies claim 20% of wages, capped at $8,000 monthly, for flexi-time workers with children, if used to employ more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But this is not attractive enough for employers, especially given the availability of foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We propose to allow companies to claim from the Government 20% of the wages, capped at $8,000 per month, paid to any flexi-time workers with children, on condition that these money are used to employ more full-time or flexi-time workers.

sections.label: Allowance for full-time caregivers
sections.summary: PSP proposes a $1,250 monthly allowance to one parent or grandparent registered as full-time caregiver of a Singapore Citizen child from birth to age seven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP proposes that the Government pay a $1,250 monthly allowance to one parent or grandparent who is registered as full-time caregiver of a Singapore Citizen child from birth until age seven.

sections.label: Scheme payouts for homemaker and grandparent
sections.summary: Under the scheme, a 35-year-old homemaker receives $1,000 cash and $462.50 CPF, while a 75-year-old grandparent receives $1,156 cash and $156 CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, a 35-year-old full-time homemaker, for example, would receive $1,000 in cash and $462.50 in CPF contributions, while a 75-year-old grandparent would receive $1,156 in cash and $156 in CPF contributions.

sections.label: PSP invitation and Leong Mun Wai amendment
sections.summary: PSP invites Singaporeans to join its journey, and Mr Leong Mun Wai proposes an amendment replacing 'continued review and updating' with 're-imagination'.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: PSP invites all Singaporeans to join us in our journey to re-imagine our policies and build a better Singapore, together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There is one amendment proposed by Mr Leong Mun Wai to the Motion: "In line 2, to delete the words 'continued review and updating' and insert 're-imagination'.".

sections.label: HDB and social agency scoring proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests HDB work with social agencies like Family Service Centres to assess applicants' difficulties and give in-principle approval before divorce is finalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What I would like to suggest for such situations is for HDB to join hands and work closely with social agencies such as Family Service Centres to conduct a more in-depth analysis and establish a scoring system to measure and assess applicants' difficulties, and whether they are in dire need of shelter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If the results of the analysis show that an applicant’s situation is serious, does not have close family support and also does not have a place to live in and so on, HDB can give "in-principle approval" even though the divorce has not been officially finalised.

sections.label: Thorough evaluation for ICA appeals
sections.summary: The speaker says a more thorough evaluation would help ICA assess better, noting its current process accepts appeals only via email and e-forms, without face-to-face sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By having a more thorough evaluation process, this will help ICA make more accurate and better assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is my understanding that ICA's current process only accepts appeals via email and e-forms, without any face-to-face sessions.

sections.label: Poll and survey on marriage and dating
sections.summary: The speaker cites poll and survey findings on marriage intentions, dating and social circles, and urges the Government to enable more resources for social interactions among young people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this poll, 70% of the youngest group think it is not necessary to get married, 58% of the middle group and 50% of the older group feel the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Despite this, 68% of the youngest unmarried respondents, between 21 and 34 years, old foresee themselves getting married.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In my 2023 Budget and Committee of Supply speeches, I urge the Government to go more upstream and enable more resources for social interactions among our young people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I cited then the Marriage and Parenthood Survey 2021, which found 80% of young single respondents intending to get married, but 50% of them were not dating, with 38% of this group having not dated before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among those who were not currently dating, 58% of them expressed having a limited social circle and 57% of them not having many opportunities to meet potential partners.

sections.label: Jalan Kayu Y-Connect pilot programme
sections.summary: The speaker will pilot a next step Y-Connect programme for Jalan Kayu young people in the next few months, with small donations from donors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With a good start since 2023, I will further deepen the support for Jalan Kayu young people by piloting, in the next few months, a next step Y-Connect programme, with small donations raised from donors who share my belief.

sections.label: Seoul wedding hall applications
sections.summary: Seoul accepted citizen applications to be the first couple to wed at a new event hall of about 700 square metres holding about 150 guests, with booking fees of about 100,000 to 200,000 won.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Seoul government accepted applications from Seoul citizens to become the first couple to wed at the event hall.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They publicised that the new event hall was about 700 square metres in size, could accommodate about 150 guests at a booking fee then of just about 100,000 won to 200,000 won, which is about $95 to $190.

sections.label: Piloting wedding venues at public institutions
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government can consider piloting a similar initiative, with funding support to iconic, historical and beautiful public institutions, to host a similar programme for young people desiring to get married.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can our Government consider piloting a similar initiative, with funding support to iconic, historical and beautiful public institutions like the National Gallery or the Old Parliament House, just to name a few, to host a similar programme for our young people desiring to get married?

sections.label: Hybrid queue and ballot pilot
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MND can consider piloting a hybrid system of queue plus ballot for first-timer couples who have failed after one to two tries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I fully understand the reasons and principles of fairness upheld by the Ministry of National Development (MND) and the HDB for the current ballot system, I wonder if MND can consider piloting a hybrid system of queue plus ballot for first-timer couples who have failed after one to two tries.

sections.label: Couples caring for senior parents
sections.summary: Each of these couples are working individuals with senior parents in their 60s and 70s to care for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Each of these couples are also working individuals and with senior parents in their 60s and 70s to care for.

sections.label: Marriage bond and sacrifices
sections.summary: A common theme from these couples is a strong marriage bond and personal sacrifices as husbands and wives over the years of courtship, marriage and parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A common theme that emerged from these couples is a strong marriage bond and personal sacrifices as husbands and wives for each other over the years of courtship, marriage and parenthood.

sections.label: No lost generations on marriage
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore's TFR fell to a record low of 0.97 in 2023, but the residents and friends interviewed made the speaker realise there are no lost generations who do not want marriage or parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While Singapore's TFR has fallen to another record low of 0.97 in 2023, 51 years after I was born, the residents and friends whom I have interviewed for this speech, especially the last group, made me realised that we do not have lost generations who do not want marriage or parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We just have many good policies and initiatives still to be implemented and good stories still to be told.

sections.label: Falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR fell below one in 2023, raising economic and social concerns and a projected old age support ratio of 2.7 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our TFR fell below one for the first time in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is not just a concern economically in our ageing society, due to a shrinking local workforce which demands supplementary talent as we strive to remain competitive in a turbulent world, but also socially, as demographic changes affect the composition and fabric of our society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It also results in more Singaporeans being sandwiched, with the old age support ratio projected to decrease to 2.7 in 2030.

sections.label: Working couples and gender roles
sections.summary: A 2020 census found 52.5% of couples have both parents working, and a study found Singaporeans emphasise egalitarian gender relationships less than Spain or Norway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to a 2020 Singapore Population Census, the percentage of couples with both parents working is 52.5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In particular, as women today see unprecedented levels of self-autonomy and financial independence, they desire a shared partnership instead of reinforced gender roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, a study which polled more than 22,000 people in eight countries, found that Singaporeans do not place as much emphasis on egalitarian gender relationships in a marriage as people in other countries, such as Spain or Norway.

sections.label: Infertility among Singapore couples
sections.summary: Infertility, defined by WHO as inability to conceive after one year, affects about 15% of couples in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Defined by World Health Organization as a couple's inability to conceive after one year, infertility currently affects about 15% of couples in Singapore.

sections.label: Cost of fertility treatment
sections.summary: Various hospital websites state the cost can range from $7,000 to $15,000, amounts that make most think carefully before pursuing this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Various hospital websites state that the cost can range from $7,000 to $15,000, amounts that would make most of us think carefully before pursuing this.

sections.label: Rise in IVF cases
sections.summary: A Straits Times article reported KK Women's and Children's Hospital recorded over 40% more IVF cases between 2014 and 2023, with hospitals ramping up capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A Straits Time article published that KK Women's and Children's Hospital has recorded more than 40% increase in IVF cases between 2014 and 2023, and that hospitals are ramping up capacity to support assisted reproductive treatments.

sections.label: October 2024 BTO application rates
sections.summary: The October 2024 sales exercise showed a median application rate of 2.6 for first-time families, with Central Trio at Ang Mo Kio at 4.1.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recent October 2024 sales exercise revealed that the median application rate for first-time families was 2.6, with the Central Trio at Ang Mo Kio being 4.1.

sections.label: 3Gen units subsidies and allocation
sections.summary: Speaker seeks continued subsidies for elderly moving into 3Gen units and notes priority allocation for families with greater needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It would also be helpful if elderly who do not have much savings are able to continue receiving certain subsidies or reliefs, which they would have otherwise enjoyed if they are still staying in their own flats, should they choose to move into these 3Gen units with their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am grateful for this option, which has grown in popularity in recent years and been a lifeline for families, married couples, applicants under the fiancé-fiancée scheme and divorced or widowed parents with children, the latter being a family unit, often going through much pain and changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also note that the Government has ramped up supply dramatically, with the intention to double the amount of available units to 4,000 this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, the Government considers families with greater needs first, couples with at least one child, including expectant parents, get priority in the allocation of flats.

sections.label: Open Market vouchers take-up and rental subsidy
sections.summary: Speaker asks about take-up rate of Open Market vouchers since July 2024 and proportion of flat rental cost subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could the Government also share how the take up rate of the Open Market vouchers has been since its launch in July 2024 and what is the proportion of the average 4-room and 3-room flat unit rental cost that is subsidised by the Open Market vouchers?

sections.label: PSP calls to reduce cost of living
sections.summary: PSP repeats four calls: reduce GST to 7%, price HDB flats without land cost, manage property and hawker rents, and Government pay MediShield Life premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the cost of living issue has been raised in this House many times before, I will today simply repeat the major calls PSP has made previously to reduce cost of living: one, reduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) back to 7% and exempt basic necessities; two, pricing HDB flats without land cost, unless sold in resale market; three, manage property prices and rents, and in particular, reduce rents at hawker centres; and four, MediShield Life premiums to be paid by the Government.

sections.label: S Pass quota and parental leave
sections.summary: Speaker suggests reducing S Pass quota to 9% for all employers and giving additional quotas to employers with employees on parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To illustrate, we can reduce the quota for S Pass from 10% to, say, 9% for all employers and give additional quotas to employers with employees going on parental leave.

sections.label: ART treatment cycles and co-funding
sections.summary: About 10,500 ART cycles were carried out in Singapore in 2022, with Government co-funding up to 75% for eligible couples under age 40.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on the latest available data, about 10,500 cycles of ART treatments were carried out in Singapore in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, the Government provides up to 75% in co-funding for couples going through ART at public hospitals, who are under age 40 and have been assessed by a doctor to have met the clinical requirements for ART.

sections.label: Israel IVF public funding
sections.summary: Israel has the world's highest per capita IVF rate because its government fully funds unlimited IVF cycles for women under 45 until two children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Israel has the world's highest per capita rate of IVF procedures and fertility clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is because the Israeli government provides full public funding for an unlimited number of IVF cycles for any Israeli woman under age 45 until she has two children with her current male partner.

sections.label: PSP co-funding for trans-national couples
sections.summary: PSP proposes up to 75% co-funding for assisted conception procedures if one spouse is a Singapore Citizen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP believes we can do more to support trans-national couples to start their fertility journey, especially since any child born out of such marriages will be a Singapore Citizen by birth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thus, PSP proposes that all couples can receive up to 75% co-funding for assisted conception procedures, as long as one spouse is a Singapore Citizen.

sections.label: PSP unlimited ART co-funding proposal
sections.summary: PSP proposes co-funding unlimited ART cycles for women under 40 until they have two Singapore Citizen children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even if the Government provided the maximum $7,700 funding for all 10,500 ART cycles carried out in Singapore in 2022, the total cost to the Government would be less than $81 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP believes that we should co-fund unlimited ART cycles for women under the age of 40, until they have two children who are Singapore Citizens.

sections.label: PSP employer and fertility support proposals
sections.summary: PSP proposes employer incentives, parent subsidies, ART subsidies and egg freezing support, and asks the Government to consider them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We also proposed that the Government should increase efforts to encourage employers to support employees with FWAs, allow family-friendly employers to receive relatively higher foreign worker quotas, provide subsidies for full-time parents or grandparents caring for young children, increase subsidies for ART treatment and better support women who choose to freeze their eggs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We hope the Government will seriously consider our proposals and reimagine current policies to address the issue of continuously declining birth rate. : We hope the Government will seriously consider our proposals to lower cost of living, provide employer incentives, more SWT flats and greater financial support for fertility treatments and egg freezing, to support Singaporeans in their parenthood aspirations.

sections.label: Survey on reasons for not having children
sections.summary: A National Population and Talent Division survey shows economic burden and high child-raising costs as main concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The survey by our National Population and Talent Division shows that the main reason for married people not having children is the economic burden, which is 64% of the respondents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But the main concern of singles is that the cost of raising children is too high, which is 89%.

sections.label: Housing subsidies and shorter waiting times
sections.summary: The passage proposes higher housing subsidies for young couples and building HDB flats in advance to cut waiting time to about 18 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We can also increase the housing subsidies for young couples under a certain age, in order to encourage them to get married early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We can shorten the waiting time for home buyers and start building HDB flats in advance, based on the number of first-time applicants and the average number of marriages yearly in recent years, therefore reducing the waiting time to about 18 months.

sections.label: Government paternity and parental leave
sections.summary: The passage commends Government efforts and notes paid mandatory paternity leave and Shared Parental Leave increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I commend and endorse our Government's continuous efforts over the last few decades to build a "Singapore Made for Families".

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is heartening to note that from April, the Government will pay for four weeks of mandatory paternity leave and an additional six weeks of mandatory Shared Parental Leave, with the latter increasing to 10 weeks from April next year.

sections.label: Social networking, couples, preschool subsidies
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would run a vetted social networking agency and app, and urges more subsidies for younger couples and more places and lower fees in Government-supported preschools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider running a social networking agency and app, where participants and organised activities are screened and vetted?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For younger couples under the age of 30, they have less time to accumulate savings and this concern may lead them to postpone having children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider providing more subsidies for this group for pre-natal care and deliveries at our public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry of Education (MOE) provide more places and lower fees in Government-supported preschools?

sections.label: Subsidies for grandparent care
sections.summary: States that government subsidies may be helpful to certain families which prefer their grandparents to look after their grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The government subsidies may be helpful to certain families which prefer their grandparents to look after their grandchildren.

sections.label: Singaporeans value family highly
sections.summary: States that over 90% of Singaporeans polled by the IPS for its global World Values Survey 2020 valued family as very important, compared to less than 40% for other facets of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, over 90% of Singaporeans polled by the IPS for its global World Values Survey 2020, valued family as "very important", compared to less than 40% for other facets of life such as work, friends and leisure time.

sections.label: Safeguards against algorithmic management
sections.summary: Urges the Government to consider requiring companies that apply AI to decisions affecting workers to disclose safeguards, whistle-blowing avenues and recourse upholding non-discriminatory, responsible AI use.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the rise in algorithmic management of workers, it is timely for a refreshed social compact to include safeguards that protect workers against exploitative algorithmic management practices that could arise when the business environment becomes complex and uncertain.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would thus like to urge the Government to consider requiring companies that apply artificial intelligence (AI) to decisions affecting workers, such as ride hailing and delivery platform operators, to provide transparent disclosure of the safeguards, whistle-blowing avenues and recourse in place to uphold non-discriminatory and responsible use of AI for decision-making that impacts workers.

sections.label: Support for freelance creative professionals
sections.summary: Urges the Government to support local freelance creative professionals' capability development and the creative industry by requiring principal creative agencies engaged by Government Ministries or agencies to prioritise engaging Singaporean creative freelancers or enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To further save costs, these companies are also offshoring entry-level creative work activities to lower-cost countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These forces have brought upheaval to the creative work value chain in Singapore and has affected a big swathe of local creative freelancers, some of whom had experienced up to a 30% drop in their income from creative work.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the increase in such external pressures on Singaporean freelance creative professionals, it is timely for a refreshed social compact to provide safe spaces for Singaporean creative professionals to unlearn and re-learn, so as level up their thinking and technology-adoption in tandem with the opening of new avenues to monetise creative talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would thus like to urge the Government to take the lead in supporting the capability development of our local freelance creative professionals and the development of Singapore's creative industry, by requiring principal creative agencies engaged by Government Ministries or agencies for creative projects to prioritise engaging Singaporean creative freelancers or enterprises for specialised expertise needed.

sections.label: GenAI, low-wage jobs, food services
sections.summary: Cites a July 2023 McKinsey Global Institute report on GenAI eliminating low-wage US food and customer service jobs by 2030 and Singapore's 2023 Jobs Transformation Map for food services.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In July 2023, the McKinsey Global Institute published a report which found that many low-wage jobs in the food industry and in customer service in the US could be eliminated by GenAI by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The same study suggests that workers in lower-wage jobs are up to 14 times more likely to need to change occupations than those in highest-wage positions and most will need additional skills to do so successfully.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the 2023 edition of the Government's Jobs Transformation Map for food services sector highlighted the urgency to redesign food services jobs to make the sector attractive to Singaporeans.

sections.label: Social compact for workers
sections.summary: A Singapore Made for Families must be anchored by a refreshed social compact boosting over-500,000 platform workers, freelancers and low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A "Singapore Made for Families" must therefore be anchored by a refreshed and renewed social compact that would give a boost to the livelihood skills and opportunities of our over-500,000 Singaporean platform workers, creative freelancers and low-wage workers facing the advancement of emerging technologies and economic renewal.

sections.label: South Korea and Finland examples
sections.summary: South Korea introduced Digital Detox Zones and camps, while Finland prioritises outdoor play in schools.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Countries like South Korea and Finland have set an example.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: South Korea has introduced "Digital Detox Zones" and camps, while Finland prioritises outdoor play in schools.

sections.label: Delaying social media use
sections.summary: The speaker shares three considerations for protecting youths and urges delaying social media use until at least age 16.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Building on these efforts, I would like to share three key considerations for better protecting our youths in today's digital landscape.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge parents and teens alike to consider delaying social media use until at least age 16, or for as long as possible.

sections.label: Studying Australia's social media ban
sections.summary: Singapore is currently studying Australia's proposed ban on social media for those under 16.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore is currently studying Australia's proposed ban on social media for those under 16.

sections.label: CCAs and primary school trials
sections.summary: The CCA system lays a strong foundation for youth development and MOE's removal of primary school CCA trials is commendable.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our co-curricular activities (CCAs) system lays a strong foundation for youth development and MOE's recent decision to remove primary school CCA trials is a commendable step forward.

sections.label: Proposed Disconnect to Connect Week
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a Disconnect to Connect Week for students to disconnect from social media, citing a US teen experiment.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Just as Earth Hour gives our planet a much-needed break and Home-based Learning Day prepares students for remote learning, I propose the introduction of Disconnect to Connect Week, a dedicated week for students to disconnect from social media and replace it with real-world social connections.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: A recent experiment involving a group of US teens who swapped their smartphones for flip phones for just seven days yielded striking results.

sections.label: Compulsory parent digital boundary workshops
sections.summary: Schools could consider making workshops on healthy digital boundaries compulsory for parents, beyond IMDA's Digital for Life resources.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Beyond IMDA's Digital for Life resources, schools could consider making workshops on healthy digital boundaries compulsory for parents.

sections.label: Leave for disabled children's parents
sections.summary: It proposes extending childcare leave for parents of children with disabilities with high support needs to at least age 18, and more paid leave days.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: May we explore considerations for parents caring for children with disabilities who require long-term medical care?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I propose extending childcare leave for parents of children with disabilities with high support needs, to at least age 18.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In addition, I urge the Government to increase the number of paid leave days per year for them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: If extending leave is not feasible, FWAs should be legislated, with medical certification required to prevent abuse.

sections.label: Jobs and FWAs for caregivers
sections.summary: It urges the Government to allocate resources and work with employers on job opportunities offering FWAs for caregivers, whose accommodations are not legislated.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given that reasonable accommodations for this group are still not legislated, I urge the Government to allocate resources and collaborate with employers to create job opportunities that offer FWAs, while also recognising and leveraging the professional expertise of these caregivers.

sections.label: More affordable full-day childcare
sections.summary: It suggests raising the Basic Subsidy for full-day childcare by $100 and reducing the minimum co-payment for median- and low-income households by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, I hope the Government can make full-day childcare even more affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I suggest to raise the Basic Subsidy for full-day childcare by $100, and correspondingly, reduce the minimum co-payment for median- and low-income households by $100.

sections.label: CDA funds covering childcare fees
sections.summary: It says median-income parents contributing $4,000 to the CDA, with matching and First-Step Grant, get $13,000, covering four years of Anchor Operator fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, my suggestion is that median-income parents who contribute $4,000 to the CDA, with $4,000 matching from the Government plus the First-Step Grant of $5,000 also from the Government, making a total of $13,000 in the CDA, should be able to cover four full years of full-day childcare fees at an Anchor Operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This works out to a fee of around $250 per month, which is also why I suggested earlier to raise the Basic Subsidy by $100 and to reduce the minimum co-payment, by $100, so that the co-payment at the median-income level can be brought down to around $250.

sections.label: Cost of proposed childcare subsidies
sections.summary: It states the suggested higher childcare subsidies will cost the Government at most $200 million more each year, and the Child Development Bonus around $200 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The higher childcare subsidies that I have suggested will cost the Government at most $200 million more each per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Whereas the Child Development Bonus that I have suggested will also cost around $200 million per year.

sections.label: Student care fee assistance tiers
sections.summary: Student care costs between $5 and $120 per child monthly after Government fee assistance for lowest income decile families, depending on small income differences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But there are seven tiers of fee assistance for student care, even for families within the lowest income decile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, student care can cost as little as $5 per child per month, or as much as $120 per child per month, after Government fee assistance for these families within the lowest income decile, depending on very small differences in their income levels.

sections.label: Proposals for affordable childcare and bonus
sections.summary: The passage proposes $5 and $25 monthly student care fees for the lowest two income deciles, higher childcare subsidies, and a $600 yearly Child Development Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: As importantly, there is much scope for us to make student care a lot more affordable for lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think student care should cost only $5 per child per month for all families in the lowest income decile; and $25 per month per child, not $250, for families in the next income decile, 11th to 20th percentile, just like full-day childcare is costing today, after subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: One, make full-day childcare even more affordable; raise the Basic Subsidy for full-day childcare by $100; reduce the minimum co-payment for median- and lower-income households by $100; and refresh our benchmark for affordable childcare – $4,000 contribution from parents into the CDA should be able to cover four full years of childcare from three to six years old, with Government grant and maximum Government matching, if you are at median income and your child is with an Anchor Operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Two, give every school-going Singaporean child, between seven and 16 years old, a "Child Development Bonus" of $600, in cash, each year.

sections.label: Marriage and parenting movement expansion
sections.summary: The movement has expanded to 18 towns, letting many families benefit from marriage and parenting programmes and resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The movement has since expanded to 18 towns, allowing many families to benefit from an extensive range of marriage and parenting programmes and resources.

sections.label: Preschool hours due to work
sections.summary: The brief reported that close to 40% of preschool children in Singapore spend more than 50 hours a week in preschools due to parents' long working hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The brief reported that close to 40% of preschool children in Singapore spend more than 50 hours a week in preschools, due to their parents' long working hours.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory on workplace mental health
sections.summary: In 2023, MOM enhanced the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces to include an after-hours work communication policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2023, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) enhanced the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces to include the establishment of an after-hours work communication policy.

sections.label: Relief Staff Pool for preschools
sections.summary: Teachers in short-staffed preschools struggle to find time for bathroom breaks or lunch, so ECDA launched the Relief Staff Pool initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In preschools that are constantly short-staffed, some teachers tell me that they even find it hard to find time to go to the bathroom or to have their lunch during working hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I was, therefore, glad when ECDA launched the Relief Staff Pool initiative to help preschools access affordable and reliable relief staff services.

sections.label: Early childhood educator pay increase
sections.summary: Pay for early childhood educators rose between 10% and 30% in recent years, alongside the Relief Staff Pool and removal of mandatory Saturday classes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In addition to the Relief Staff Pool initiative and the removal of mandatory Saturday classes, the pay for early childhood educators has also increased in recent years by between 10% and 30%.

sections.label: Preschool enrolment for three to four year olds
sections.summary: MSF statistics show nine in 10 children aged three to four are enrolled in preschool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to statistics by MSF, nine in 10 children aged three to four years old are enrolled in a preschool.

sections.label: Lower-income preschool participation and subsidies
sections.summary: Preschool participation for lower-income children is eight in 10, and MSF was urged to give more subsidies and incorporated preschool requirements under ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: When it comes to children from lower-income families, the preschool participation rate drops to eight in 10 children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I urge MSF to provide greater preschool subsidies for our lower-income families and improve their accessibility to parenting resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I was glad when MSF incorporated preschool requirements under the ComLink+ Progress Package to encourage participating families to send their children to preschool.

sections.label: SMEs supporting families and employment
sections.summary: SMEs contribute 70% of local employment and form the backbone of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMEs are often underappreciated when it comes to their role in supporting families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They are the silent engines of our economy, contributing 70% of local employment and forming the backbone of our society.

sections.label: Manpower concerns and demand uncertainty
sections.summary: The SPF National Business Survey shows 37% of businesses cite manpower availability as a key concern, with SME demand uncertainty rising from 30% in 2023 to 40% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SPF National Business Survey confirms this, with 37% of businesses reflecting that the availability of manpower remain a key concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For SMEs, these challenges are even more acute, compounded by customer demand uncertainty, which has risen sharply from 30% in 2023 to 40% in 2024.

sections.label: Support for SMEs with returning employees
sections.summary: SMEs incur extra costs when returning employees and temporary staff overlap, and the Government was urged to consider extended pay coverage for one to two months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMEs often incur additional cost during overlapping periods when both returning employees and temporary staff are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I spoke on this issue and, again, I continue to urge the Government to consider introducing support measures, such as extended pay coverage for returning employees for one to two months.

sections.label: Prioritising family-friendly businesses
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to prioritise businesses meeting family-friendly benchmarks through procurement advantages or temporary foreign work pass enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Motion presents an opportune moment to reinforce that call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider prioritising businesses that meet family-friendly benchmarks by granting them advantages, such as expanded prioritisation in Government procurement processes or temporary enhancements to foreign work pass access.

sections.label: Family and career investments
sections.summary: The speaker says family and career aspirations are mutually reinforcing and applauds plans to add 40,000 infant and childcare places in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A society with aspirations for family and career are not at odds but mutually reinforcing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I applaud the Government for making significant investments towards such a future and our plans to add 40,000 new infants and childcare places in the next five years in partnership with five Anchor Operators, demonstrating a long-term commitment to supporting families.

sections.label: National Business Survey results
sections.summary: The National Business Survey shows 40% of businesses are satisfied with the business climate while 66% cite manpower costs as the top challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent National Business Survey results show that while 40% of businesses are satisfied with the current business climate, 66% still consider manpower costs as the top challenge.

sections.label: Rising business costs risk
sections.summary: The passage states that disproportionately rising business costs or productivity not matching demands risk losing competitive edge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the cost of doing business here rise disproportionately or if productivity does not match rising demands, we risk losing our competitive edge.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood survey findings
sections.summary: A survey of 1,000 respondents identified prioritising flexible work arrangements for parents, affordable childcare and healthcare, and financial assistance as top priorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A recently concluded marriage and parenthood survey conducted by the NTUC Women and Family Unit and PAP Women's Wing, from 17 December 2024 to 9 January 2025 with 1,000 respondents, revealed key actions we can take to encourage childbearing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The top priorities identified were: one, prioritising FWAs for parents, 77% of respondents said they wanted that; two, improving access to affordable childcare and healthcare services, 74.0%; and three, increasing financial assistance and subsidies for families, 72.2%.

sections.label: Tripartite flexible work guidelines
sections.summary: The launch of the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements in April 2024 is described as a significant milestone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The launch of the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements in April 2024 is a significant milestone in this effort.

sections.label: Normalising flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: With over 70% of Singapore companies offering FWAs, the focus must be to normalise FWAs and requests for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To this end, with more than 70% of Singapore companies already offering one form of FWAs, the focus going forward must be to normalise FWAs and the requests for FWAs.

sections.label: SMEs, parental leave, childcare leave
sections.summary: It urges Government support for SMEs so employees can take parental leave securely, and monitoring of whether six days of childcare leave suffices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With SMEs employing up to 70% of the Singaporean workforce, I urge the Government to explore solutions that will support SMEs in this area so that employees can take parental leave with the peace of mind that their jobs remain secure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While we understand that both parents can take turns to share childcare responsibilities for these eight days of closure, we also recognise that young children tend to fall sick often or just have their off-days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We call on the Government to monitor feedback on whether the current provision of six days of Government-paid childcare leave remains sufficient, vis-à-vis the accessibility and utilisation of FWAs to meet our growing childcare needs.

sections.label: C U Back at Work Programme
sections.summary: NTUC's Women and Family Unit introduced the 2023 programme helping caregivers, especially women, return to work with FWAs, flexible training and pay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In view of this, the NTUC Women and Family Unit introduced the "C U Back at Work" Programme in 2023, which helps caregivers, especially women, return to work with FWAs and flexible training schedules and, of course, an attractive pay package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have close to 1,000 cubbies, as we call them, in the programme since and in 2025, we plan to expand this programme to reach more employers and roles, including PMET ones, making these opportunities available to more return-to-work moms.

sections.label: Divorce effects on children
sections.summary: MSF's 2020 research shows children of divorced parents were less likely to obtain degrees, earned less, had lower CPF and higher divorce likelihood.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: On divorce, MSF's research on Inter-generational Effects of Divorce on Children in Singapore, published in 2020, shows a clear correlation that, compared to children whose parents remained married, those whose parents were divorced, were less likely to obtain a university degree, earned less and had lower CPF balances, were less likely to get married themselves and were themselves more likely to undergo divorce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: It was clear from the report that there is a long tail in terms of the impact of broken families on children and young people, including their eventual likelihood of maintaining stability in their own lives as well as in their own future marriages and relationships.

sections.label: Support for single-parent families
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government continually reviews and updates policies supporting single-parent, blended and step-families and their children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: My first hope is that the Government continually reviews and updates its policies to support specifically single-parent families, blended or step-families, as well as children in such families.

sections.label: Strengthening extended family and kinship
sections.summary: The speaker seeks policy support to strengthen grandparenting and extended family kinship, which housing and policy strategies have not replicated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: While families can be nudged and encouraged from within, for example, through Baby Bonuses and better shared paternity and maternity packages, I wish we could do more to buttress nuclear families from outside-in, by strengthening grandparenting as well as the concept of kinship arising from the extended family, such that these too can benefit from the Government's policy support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: To some extent, the part of a kampung or village that we have not been able to replace and replicate, as effectively through our current housing and policy strategies, is this concept of extended family and kinship.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: What I mean is the support and interwoven structures and bonds that a nuclear family used to have vis-à-vis the extended family, such as grandparents, uncles and aunts who used to exist in a very close proximity and who were within reach previously.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: This is something I think is worth looking into as a policy, to establish levers where help outside the nuclear family, but within the extended family, can be encouraged, reinforced and nudged to be more forthcoming.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: In fact, I argue that this is not merely an instrument of practical caregiving support when both parents are at work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: It functions as yet another multi-layered social scaffold: one, for our families to remain intact and tightly knit against the threat of social challenges and divorce rates; two, to further impart our traditions, our cultures and our heritage to our young alongside their lived experience of modernity and technology; and three, to nourish genuine relationships and close kinships in our families as part of a building of cohesive society and a united nation.

sections.label: Support for Motion in original form
sections.summary: The speaker rises in full support of the Motion in its original form, notwithstanding earlier comments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my comments, I rise in full of support of this Motion in its original form.

sections.label: Government-Paid Parental Leave entitlements
sections.summary: New parents receive 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave, four weeks of Paternity Leave and up to six weeks of shared parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: For example, our new parents enjoy 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave, four weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave and up to six weeks of shared paternal parental leave.

sections.label: Elective egg freezing legalised in 2023
sections.summary: Singapore legalised elective egg freezing in 2023 for women aged 21 to 37 regardless of marital status, but high cost remains a barrier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Government took a significant step forward in 2023 by legalising elective egg freezing for women aged 21 to 37, regardless of marital status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: However, the high cost, estimated at $10,000 per cycle, remains a substantial barrier for many women.

sections.label: Salary gap for mothers in 40s
sections.summary: In Singapore, a woman in her 40s with at least one child earns a median gross monthly salary $1,000 less than a woman without children and $1,000 lower than a man's median income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: In Singapore, the median gross monthly salary for a woman with at least one child in their 40s is $1,000 less than woman without children and $1,000 lower than a man's median income.

sections.label: Fatherhood wage premium
sections.summary: Men tend to increase their work hours and receive the bonus when they have children, known as the fatherhood wage premium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: Men tend to increase their work hours and receive the bonus when they have children, a phenomenon also known as fatherhood wage premium.

sections.label: Flexible work and career breaks
sections.summary: With FWAs more common, companies could redesign higher-level jobs for flexible or reduced hours while still allowing promotion, and explore structured career breaks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: With FWAs becoming more common, companies could re-design higher-level jobs, so that they allow flexible or reduced hours and workloads, but still offer the possibility of promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: They can also explore structured career breaks – where a mother can take a leave of absence for say, a couple of years and be assured that she still has a job when she returns.

sections.label: Employers offering returnship programmes
sections.summary: Employers like DBS and Jacobs in Singapore have started offering returnship programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
sentences.text: In Singapore, employers like DBS and Jacobs have started offering "returnship" programmes too.

sections.label: Cost of living survey findings
sections.summary: A June 2024 Blackbox Research survey found 52% named cost of living their primary concern, with 28% more applications from ages 40 to 59.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, a survey by Blackbox Research in June 2024, found that 52% of respondents identified "cost of living" as their primary concern.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Individuals aged 40 to 59 have seen a 28% increase in application, with average loans of $22,000.

sections.label: Women and caregiving responsibilities
sections.summary: MSF says 60% of informal caregivers are women, and a 2020 Ipsos survey found women more likely to manage housework and leave jobs for caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, according to MSF, 60% of informal caregivers are women.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, a 2020 survey by Ipsos showed that women in dual-income households, were five times more likely than men to manage housework and caregiving responsibilities and nearly four times more likely to have left their jobs for caregiving purposes.

sections.label: Student academic stress study
sections.summary: A 2022 National Institute of Education study found 90% of secondary students reported academic stress from competitive education and societal expectations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2022 study by the National Institute of Education showed that 90% of secondary school students in Singapore reported experiencing stress related to their academic work and that this stress stemmed from the competitive educational environment and high societal expectations placed on academic success.

sections.label: Parental phubbing and behavioural issues
sections.summary: The study found 51% of young people experiencing frequent parental phubbing had increased behavioural issues including depression, aggression and mobile phone addiction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The study also found that 51% of the young people who experienced frequent parental phubbing, had increased behavioural issues, including depression, aggression and mobile phone addiction.

sections.label: Millennials on having children
sections.summary: A 2021 TODAY online survey indicated only 44% of Singaporean millennials sampled felt having children was important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An online survey by TODAY released in 2021 indicated that only 44% of a sample of Singaporean millennials felt that it was important to have children.

sections.label: Corporate Family Responsibility Certification and time banking
