sections.summary: Proposes Corporate Family Responsibility Certification for family-friendly policies and a community time banking system for trading family services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, introduce Corporate Family Responsibility Certification for companies that implement family-friendly policies, including FWAs; equal paid maternal and paternal leave; free on-site or subsidised childcare; family care leave, including elder care leave; reproductive leave and free employment assistance programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, establish a community time banking system where families can trade time and skills, such as babysitting, meal preparation, elderly care, transportation, house cleaning or home repairs.

sections.label: Seeking families' views on policies
sections.summary: States agencies should seek and act on the views of families of all descriptions when reviewing policies and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In reviewing and updating policies and programmes, it is important that agencies seek the views and wishes of families and potential families of all descriptions, and that these views and wishes are respectfully considered and acted upon.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Developing policies in isolation, or in response to a perceived or preferred reality, is ineffective and expensive.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It might be helpful to gain an accurate and representative picture of the contemporary preferences, hopes, concerns and needs of current and future Singaporean families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is important that we review and update this plan and in doing so, that we seek input from across the community and from across the spectrum of Singaporean families.

sections.label: What Singapore families truly need
sections.summary: Describes family as a great gift and responsibility, and names home, security, time and community as what families need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is one of life's greatest gifts, but also one of its greatest responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And for too many families in Singapore today, those challenges are becoming harder to bear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, today, let us talk about what our families truly need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The things that matter most: a home, a sense of security, time to nurture relationships and a community to lean on.

sections.label: Home ownership dream slipping away
sections.summary: States families grow and build futures there, but home ownership may be slipping out of reach for many young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is where families grow, support one another and build their futures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But for far too many young Singaporeans, the dream of home ownership may be slipping further out of reach.

sections.label: Increasing childcare leave provisions
sections.summary: Hopes to increase childcare leave on a per child basis and extend the six days to children up to age 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has been more than a decade since we increased our childcare leave provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope we can increase childcare leave and provide it on a per child basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also hope we can extend the current childcare leave provisions of six days to all children up to the age of 12 years.

sections.label: Childcare leave for young children
sections.summary: States working parents with children under seven years old can take up to six days of childcare leave yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Working parents with children under seven years old can take up to six days of childcare leave every year.

sections.label: Extend childcare leave to 12
sections.summary: The speaker asks that childcare leave be extended to all children up to age 12, instead of the current age of seven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second ask is that we extend childcare leave for all children up to the age of 12, instead of the current age of seven.

sections.label: Gap in childcare leave policy
sections.summary: The speaker says not all children go to student care or have helpers, and asks to extend childcare leave to age 12 for working parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Do we really think that primary school students can go home and stay home on their own when schools close or close early?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must remember that not all children go to student care and not all families have helpers to look after their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is a gap in our policy and for the sake of working parents, we ought to address this gap and extend childcare leave to all children up to the age of 12.

sections.label: Increase childcare leave per child
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for more childcare leave provisions provided on a per child basis, noting this has not been reviewed for over a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is always a compromise and you feel like you are never doing enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope we can do a little more for all parents by increasing our childcare leave provisions and providing it on a per child basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Again, this we have not reviewed for over a decade now.

sections.label: Flexible options for working fathers
sections.summary: The speaker says fathers may fear professional consequences for taking leave, and employers should offer flexible options without stigma, citing Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While paternity leave has been expanded in recent years, some fathers may still feel the pressure to return to work quickly or fear professional consequences or judgement from others if they take full advantage of the leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Employers should offer more flexible options for working fathers, such as part-time work, work-from-home or extended paternity leave, without stigma.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I believe that the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests that was rolled out recently will come in very useful in this regard.

sections.label: Beyond baby bonuses for families
sections.summary: The speaker says building Singapore into a conducive place for families is not just about baby bonuses and requires resolving pain points and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But this will take time and mindset shifts do not take place overnight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have to realise that building Singapore into a conducive place for families is not just about baby bonuses and, while monetary support is important and must continue, we also need to look into resolving pain points and challenges that may deter people from taking the next step in becoming parents.

sections.label: Early childhood sector expenditure doubled
sections.summary: The Government's annual expenditure on the early childhood sector has more than doubled, from $1 billion in 2018 to over $2 billion today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government's annual expenditure on the early childhood sector has more than doubled, from $1 billion in 2018, to over $2 billion today.

sections.label: Household income ceiling raised
sections.summary: In 2020 the household income ceiling for means-tested subsidies rose from $7,500 to $12,000, with subsidy quantum increased across all eligible income tiers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2020, we raised the household income ceiling for means-tested subsidies from $7,500 to $12,000 and increased the subsidy quantum across all eligible income tiers, so that more families could benefit.

sections.label: Middle-income infant care fees
sections.summary: A household earning $8,000 monthly pays about $500 per month for full-day infant care in an Anchor Operator preschool, about two-thirds of 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: A middle-income household with a monthly income of $8,000 currently pays around $500 per month for full-day infant care in an Anchor Operator preschool, which is around two-thirds of what they would have paid 10 years ago.

sections.label: Final childcare fee cap reduction
sections.summary: A final reduction for childcare fee caps in 2026 will make full-day Anchor Operator childcare expenses similar to primary school and after-school student care before means-tested subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As I announced last year, we will make a final reduction for childcare fee caps in 2026 such that families enrolled in full-day childcare in Anchor Operator preschools will pay similar expenses to that of primary school and after-school student care, before means-tested subsidies.

sections.label: Infant and childcare places growth
sections.summary: ECDA provides infrastructure and manpower recruitment funding in advance, and full-day infant care places grew from around 6,000 in 2015 to around 16,000 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: ECDA further supports Anchor Operators by providing infrastructure and manpower recruitment funding in advance, to prepare centres to receive children promptly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have also grown full-day infant care places nearly threefold over the past 10 years, from around 6,000 places in 2015 to around 16,000 places in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Full-day childcare places, on the other hand, have significantly increased over the past 10 years, from around 115,000 places in 2015 to around 200,000 places in 2024.

sections.label: Government-supported preschool share
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2024, Government-supported preschools grew from just over 50% of preschoolers in 2019 to 70% today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In just a short span of six years, from 2019 to 2024, we have increased Government-supported preschools to cater from just over 50% of preschoolers in 2019 to 70% today.

sections.label: Maximum subsidies for lower incomes
sections.summary: As of December 2024, families with monthly income of $6,000 and below qualify for maximum childcare subsidies for their income tier regardless of parents' employment status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As of December 2024, all families with a monthly income of $6,000 and below qualify for the maximum childcare subsidies for their income tier, regardless of the parents' employment status.

sections.label: ComLink+ Preschool Progress Package
sections.summary: The ComLink+ Progress Package for Preschool gives families $500 into their child's CDA for preschool enrolment at age three and $200 per quarter of good attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The ComLink+ Progress Package for Preschool encourages preschool enrolment and attendance by providing families with a $500 payout into their child's CDA if their child is enrolled in preschool in the year they turn three, and a further $200 payout for each quarter of good attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since August 2024, close to 1,500 ComLink+ families and their children have been placed on this package.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance
sections.summary: The Student Care Fee Assistance is a tiered subsidy scheme providing monthly subsidies of up to 98% of student care fees, capped at $290 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Student Care Fee Assistance is a tiered subsidy scheme, which provides monthly subsidies of up to 98% of student care fees, up to a maximum amount of $290 a month.

sections.label: Post-subsidy student care costs
sections.summary: Based on the median fee, post-subsidy costs may be under 1% to around 4% of household income for families earning under $3,000, and up to 6% for those earning $3,001 to $4,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Based on this median fee, post-subsidy, a family who has a monthly household income of less than $3,000 may incur a cost of less than 1% to around 4% of household income per child, while a family with a monthly household income of $3,001 to $4,500 may incur a cost of up to 6% of household income, per child.

sections.label: Baby Bonus and MediSave Grant
sections.summary: Each child can receive up to $38,000 in Baby Bonus Cash Gift and MediSave Grant for Newborns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Each child can receive up to $38,000 in Baby Bonus Cash Gift and MediSave Grant for Newborns.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood spending
sections.summary: Government spending on marriage and parenthood packages is expected to approach $7 billion in fiscal year 2026, up from $4 billion in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Considering the Government's investments in early childhood development and the upcoming enhancement to parental leave, we expect Government spending on marriage and parenthood packages to approach $7 billion in fiscal year 2026, a significant increase from the $4 billion in 2020.

sections.label: Paid parental leave and flexible work
sections.summary: With additional paternity leave and new shared parental leave, parents can enjoy up to 30 weeks of paid leave, and the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests took effect in December.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With the upcoming additional two weeks of mandatory Government-Paid Paternity Leave and the new Shared Parental Leave, parents will be able to enjoy up to 30 weeks of paid leave to care for their newborns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In December last year, the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests also came into effect.

sections.label: Flexi-time work arrangements and tripartite guidelines
sections.summary: More parents can use flexi-time work arrangements, and tripartite partners launched the Tripartite Guidelines on FWA Requests in December last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Now more parents are able to do so with flexi-time work arrangements, such as by reporting to work slightly later in the morning and catching up on work later in the day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Such arrangements are a game changer, not just for working parents, but their employers as well, as such arrangements effectively reduce disruptions at work To help employers and employees constructively discuss and land on FWAs that meet the needs of both parties, the tripartite partners launched the Tripartite Guidelines on FWA Requests in December last year.

sections.label: Legislating right to request FWAs
sections.summary: Mr Louis Chua suggested legislating the right to request FWAs, but such legislation may not lead to higher FWA adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Chua suggested legislating the right to request for FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: However, such legislation may not lead to higher FWA adoption, as employers still have the prerogative to approve or reject FWA requests based on business grounds, and we have seen that in other countries.

sections.label: SkillsFuture subsidies and credit
sections.summary: Singaporeans are eligible for up to 70% subsidy for SkillsFuture approved courses and can use SkillsFuture Credit to offset out-of-pocket fees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Singaporeans are eligible for up to 70% subsidy for SkillsFuture approved courses to upgrade their skills and can use their SkillsFuture Credit to offset the out-of-pocket fees.

sections.label: Programmes supporting female jobseekers
sections.summary: HerCareer, Women@Work and Mums@Works JumpStart Reintegration Programme support female jobseekers with employment facilitation, training and coaching.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Workforce Singapore’s HerCareer Initiative brings together employment facilitation programmes, such as Career Conversion Programmes and Mid-Career Pathways Programmes, that support female jobseekers to access available jobs, transit into new industries and job roles, and build up job-relevant skillsets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Yayasan MENDAKI's Women@Work initiative offers training in job-ready skills like interview techniques, business communication and digital literacy, as well as a support network to connect participants to job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: And there is Mums@Works JumpStart Reintegration Programme that helps women transit back to work with the help of a dedicated coach.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill discrimination grounds
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Bill passed in January this year prohibits discrimination on grounds of pregnancy, breast-feeding and caregiving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The landmark Workplace Fairness Bill which was passed in January this year prohibits such discrimination on the grounds of pregnancy and breast-feeding as well as caregiving responsibilities.

sections.label: MOE education system shifts
sections.summary: MOE removed mid-year examinations, introduced PSLE achievement level scoring, moved away from T-score and implemented full subject-based banding from 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: MOE has indeed been making bold shifts in our education system: the removal of mid-year examination at all levels in primary and secondary schools, the introduction of PSLE achievement level scoring system, moving away from "T" score, as well as the full implementation of full subject-based banding from 2024 onwards for students to customise their education at a finer level.

sections.label: Shift from academic emphasis
sections.summary: The shifts move away from over-emphasising academic performance to prioritise holistic development of students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Through these shifts and moves, we are moving away from an over-emphasis on academic performance to prioritise holistic developments of our students instead.

sections.label: MOE holistic student opportunities
sections.summary: MOE will provide opportunities to develop students holistically, including outdoor activities and shared-interest CCAs like athletics and water polo.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: MOE will provide such opportunities to develop students holistically, develop our students' diverse strengths and interests and support their well-being, including through outdoor activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We have started to enable students from different secondary schools to come together to pursue shared interests through collaborations between specific schools or through the centrally-run strategic partnership CCAs to support schools which might not have the capacity to run these CCAs on their own.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: These include CCAs in physical sports, namely, athletics and water polo.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education and Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will explore expanding this arrangement to more sports.

sections.label: Calls on families and marriage
sections.summary: One call asks Government to review policies supporting families, marriage and parenthood; another calls for a whole-of-society approach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The first calls for the Government to continue reviewing policies that will support families, marriage and parenthood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The second calls for a whole-of-society approach, which is a call to everyone else, in addition to the Government, to do our part to support families and Singaporeans' marriage and parenthood aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai has proposed an amendment to the Motion.

sections.label: Shifts to help families
sections.summary: In the last five years, major shifts and bold moves helped families secure affordable homes and manage child-raising costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On these, in the last five years, we have made major shifts and bold moves to help families secure affordable homes, manage the costs and stresses of raising children, and balance work and family responsibilities.

sections.label: Ramped up flat supply
sections.summary: Flat supply was ramped up, exceeding the 100,000 BTO commitment, with more than 50,000 flats launching from 2025 to 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In parallel, we significantly ramped up flat supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have not only met our commitment to launch 100,000 BTO flats from 2021 to 2025 but are set to exceed it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We launched 19,600 new flats last year and will launch another 19,600 BTO flats this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will continue to put out a steady pipeline of flats to meet housing demand in the next few years and are launching more than 50,000 flats between 2025 inclusive and 2027.

sections.label: Increased EHG grants
sections.summary: With the increased EHG in August 2024, a first-time married couple can get up to $120,000 for BTO and $230,000 for resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With the increased EHG in August 2024, a first-time married couple can benefit from grants of up to $120,000 for BTO flats and up to $230,000 for resale flats.

sections.label: Rental housing for divorcing couples
sections.summary: HDB already allows individuals who have commenced divorce proceedings to apply for rental housing before interim or final judgments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Government understands and fully empathises with the concerns of divorced couples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It may be that Mr Faisal is not aware but actually today, HDB does already allow individuals who have commenced divorce proceedings to apply for rental housing, even before the interim or final judgments are obtained.

sections.label: New flat keys collected
sections.summary: About 80,000 households would have collected keys to their new flats between 2020 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: About 80,000 households would have collected keys to their new flats between 2020 and 2024.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawal for delivery
sections.summary: For a typical two-day B2 or C Class ward delivery, MediSave withdrawal will be up to $4,280, a more than 50% increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For a typical delivery episode comprising a two-day B2 or C Class ward stay and related pre-delivery medical expenses, the amount of MediSave one can withdraw will be up to $4,280, a more than 50% increase from today.

sections.label: Baby bonus increased
sections.summary: The MGN will be increased from $4,000 to $5,000 for babies born on or after 1 April this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The MGN will be increased from $4,000 to $5,000 for babies born on or after 1 April this year.

sections.label: Education subsidies per child
sections.summary: Every Singaporean child can receive over $200,000 in education subsidies from preschool through to secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In total, every Singaporean child can receive over $200,000 in education subsidies from preschool through to secondary school.

sections.label: Parental leave and father protection
sections.summary: Unpaid Infant Care Leave doubled to 12 days, 10 weeks Shared Parental Leave added, 30 weeks total paid leave, and employment protection for fathers from 1 April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We doubled Unpaid Infant Care Leave to 12 days per parent per year, in the child's first two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have introduced 10 additional weeks of new Shared Parental Leave, with the leave equally allocated between both parents as a default to encourage shared parental responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These, together with maternity leave, gives parents of newborns a total of 30 weeks of paid leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are also introducing employment protection for fathers starting from 1 April this year, such that it will be unlawful for employers to dismiss male employees on paternity leave.

sections.label: Fertility test and IVF subsidies
sections.summary: Eligible couples can get up to 70% subsidies for fertility tests and up to 75% co-funding for Assisted Conception Procedures in public institutions, with elective egg freezing introduced in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Eligible couples can receive subsidies of up to 70% for fertility tests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Those undergoing Assisted Conception Procedures in public healthcare institutions can receive up to 75% co-funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We also introduced elective egg freezing in 2023, to give women who wish to start a family the option to do so if they marry later.

sections.label: Draft Code on Accessibility 2025
sections.summary: BCA released the Draft Code on Accessibility 2025 for public consultation, proposing enhanced requirements for lactation rooms in office buildings and business parks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On this, I am pleased to inform Mr Louis Ng and Members that the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) has recently released the Draft Code on Accessibility 2025 for public consultation which, among other things, proposes enhanced requirements for lactation rooms in office buildings and business parks.

sections.label: Made For Families business pledges
sections.summary: Over 280 businesses have pledged under the Made For Families movement, and more are encouraged to join as partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To date, more than 280 businesses have pledged their commitment under the Made For Families movement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I, therefore, encourage more businesses to join us as partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This includes for buying their first flat; grants up to $120,000 for BTO flats and up to $230,000 for resale flats; not forgetting the market subsidies that we provide to keep BTO flats affordable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It also includes support for raising children up to $38,000 in Baby Bonus and MGN for each child and over $200,000 in education subsidies per child from preschool to secondary school, and even more for higher education.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood initiative costs
sections.summary: Marriage and parenthood initiatives are expected to cost close to $7 billion in FY2026, up from over $4 billion in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: All in all, factoring our investments in the early childhood sector and upcoming parental leave enhancements, we expect marriage and parenthood initiatives to cost the Government close to $7 billion in FY2026, up from over $4 billion in 2020.

sections.label: Preschool and infant care capacity
sections.summary: Infant care capacity was tripled over 10 years, and Government-supported places will cater for 80% of preschools by year end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have enhanced access to affordable quality preschools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have ramped up the infant care capacity threefold over the last 10 years and by the end of this year, we will achieve our commitment to provide Government-supported places to cater for 80% of preschools.

sections.label: Ten weeks Government-paid leave
sections.summary: Ten weeks of Government-paid leave, under the Forward SG care pillar, will cost around $400 million per year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Ten weeks of Government-paid leave, which is going to cost us something to the tune of $400 million per year and this was under the care pillar of Forward SG.

sections.label: PSP Affordable Homes Scheme opposition
sections.summary: The speaker says PSP's Affordable Homes Scheme is a pre-paid rental scheme and a raid on the Reserves, so cannot support it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because PSP's Affordable Homes Scheme is akin to a pre-paid rental scheme that turns Singaporeans from home owners to tenants and users only have the option to buy the flat at the point when they are actually going to sell it and it is a raid on the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, for that reason, because in the context of this amendment, re-imagination entails certain policies put forward by PSP, of which a key one is the Affordable Homes Scheme, which constitutes amongst other things, a raid on the Reserves and I cannot support it.

sections.label: Divorce proceedings rental housing application
sections.summary: HDB allows individuals who have commenced divorce proceedings to apply for rental housing before interim and final judgments are obtained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I will have to confirm whether or not it is a specific scheme, but what I can confirm is what I mentioned earlier, which is that even though you have not finalised the divorce, you can still make the application.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, as I said earlier, and let me just check what I said there: "HDB does already allow individuals who have commenced divorce proceedings to apply for rental housing even before the interim and final judgments are obtained." I think this was dealt with in the reply to a previous Parliamentary Question in November 2020.

sections.label: Rental flat divorce applicants
sections.summary: For rental housing, HDB allows individuals who have commenced divorce proceedings to apply before interim or final judgments are obtained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the one that I talked about was in the context of a rental flat, because that was Mr Faisal Manap's original speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, for the rental housing, HDB does allow individuals who have commenced divorce proceedings to apply for rental housing, even before the interim or final judgments are obtained.

sections.label: HDB procedures and low TFR
sections.summary: The speaker suggests HDB's procedures could be more facilitative and asks the Minister about the low and declining TFR.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, maybe that might be a way of doing it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But perhaps, what I can do is, see whether HDB's procedures can be more facilitative, because that will help people who may not be familiar with all the various legal documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As a result of that, I have many questions to ask.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But first of all, I would like to ask the Minister, today, I think all of us agree that the low TFR and the declining TFR is a very serious problem for our country.

sections.label: HDB prices, waiting time, TFR
sections.summary: The speaker asks about HDB prices, says waiting time below three years cannot be reduced, and proposes Affordable Homes and Millennial Apartments Schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: After all the policies that the Minister has said here, how about the price of the HDB?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Two, you said you cannot reduce the waiting time to below three years; then, TFR cannot be improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, our suggestions of Affordable Homes Scheme plus our Millennial Apartments Scheme do provide a feasible solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, secondly, when you want to encourage Singaporeans, especially mothers to have babies, I think we ought to upgrade the kind of help we want to give them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, while we have done some of these and that, like before birth, you say now the MediSave is 50% increase from today.

sections.label: People engaged through exercises
sections.summary: The speaker says that counting all people engaged through the various exercises, it is almost 200,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In fact, if you take into account all the people that we have engaged through the various exercises, it is almost like 200,000 people.

sections.label: Total fertility rates by country
sections.summary: The passage lists total fertility rates for France, Denmark, Sweden, UK, Japan, Singapore and South Korea, with Singapore at 0.97 and South Korea at 0.72.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In France, it has gone down to 1.68; Denmark is 1.50; Sweden, 1.45; UK, 1.44; Japan, 1.20; Singapore, 0.97; South Korea, 0.72.

sections.label: Policies from feedback and objections
sections.summary: The passage states policies were developed in response to feedback, resulting in the reclassification framework, enhanced Baby Bonus, childcare enhancements and Shared Parental Leave, while the Affordable Homes Scheme was objected to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And so, we developed our policies specifically in response to what they told us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And this resulted in the reclassification framework, this resulted in the enhanced Baby Bonus, this resulted in the enhancements to childcare, this resulted in the Shared Parental Leave – all of the things which I outlined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The main issue I had was with his Affordable Homes Scheme because that constitutes a raid on the Reserves and has all those other downsides.

sections.label: Comparing TFR with other countries
sections.summary: The passage asks why Singapore does not compare its TFR with France and other countries that maintain above 1.5, while Singapore is 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: First of all, when we compare the global trend of TFR, why do not we compare ourselves with France, compare ourselves with those countries – because although the Minister has quoted a downward trend of the TFR as a global phenomenon, but other countries are able to maintain it at above 1.5; but we are 0.97.

sections.label: Target of 1.4 TFR
sections.summary: The passage proposes fixing a target of 1.4 TFR within the next decade, saying Singapore cannot move back to 1.8 or 2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: If we can say today that, yes, we put up a national plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But Singaporeans, I do not think we can move back up to 1.8 or 2 TFR, but let us fix a target of 1.4 within the next decade.

sections.label: Made for Families and Forward SG
sections.summary: The passage states the Government wants a Singapore Made for Families, encourages marriage and parenthood, and implemented Forward SG to look at new policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As far as this Government is concerned, we want to make a Singapore that is Made for Families and we are encouraging marriage and parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have policies in the past which took us up to a certain point.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But remember, we recognise that changes need to be made and things need to be looked at afresh – and that is exactly why we implemented Forward SG and that is why we embarked on the process of looking at what new policies we can introduce.

sections.label: Youth survey on life goals
sections.summary: The passage cites an August 2024 National Youth Council and IPS survey of 3,000 people aged 17 to 24, where marriage ranked sixth and having children lower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I just wanted to highlight another dimension to marriage and parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And I would like to cite a survey that was conducted by the National Youth Council together with the IPS, which was published in August 2024, where 3,000 young people had been surveyed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: They were aged between 17 and 24 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And in their list of priorities, I am reading from the survey here, they had prioritised their top life goals for the next five years: the first was being in good health; the second was having a good career; the third is having lots of money; the fourth is having financial security; only at number six is getting married; and having children is actually further down the list.

sections.label: Limits of setting targets
sections.summary: The speaker says some things can be encouraged and facilitated but not given a finite measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I think you made the same point twice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I mean, there are certain things where you can set targets and there are certain things where you can be as encouraging and as facilitative as possible, but I do not think that you can put a finite measure on it.

sections.label: Encouraging environment for personal decisions
sections.summary: The approach taken is to create a country, society and environment as encouraging and supportive as possible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But when it comes to emotions, when it comes to things like fertility, when it comes to personal decisions, those are very hard to quantify.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the approach that we have taken is to try and create a country, a society, an environment that is as encouraging and supportive as possible.

sections.label: Support for Singaporean families
sections.summary: The House commits to provide its utmost support to Singaporean families, and hopes the wish list materialises at Budget 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: From the responses provided by Minister of State Sun, Minister of State Gan and Minister Indranee, particularly in relation to what she has shared on BCA's Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment 2025, I feel assured to reiterate my message to fellow Singaporeans that none of you would ever be alone or should feel alone in this rewarding and fulfilling journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: And this House commits to unceasingly provide its utmost support to Singaporean families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Since, it is instead done today, on the eighth day of Chinese New Year with "eight" being associated with wealth, prosperity and success, I hope that it is an auspicious sign that the wish list that my Parliamentary colleagues and I have drawn up in our speeches for more financial support and "ang pows" for Singaporeans will materialise, perhaps even as soon as at the upcoming Budget 2025.

sections.label: Fertility health education and support
sections.summary: The villagers need fertility, health education and fertility support benefits, a point made by three named Members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: The villagers also need to be equipped with fertility, health education and fertility support benefits, a key point made by Ms Nadia Samdin, Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Desmond Choo.

sections.label: No pressure to return to work
sections.summary: No parent should feel pressure to return to work due to insufficient childcare leave or an employer refusing FWAs where feasible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, no parent, mother or father should ever feel the pressure to return to work due to them having insufficient childcare leave and/or because their employer refuses to implement FWAs where feasible.

sections.label: Mothers in the workforce
sections.summary: Mothers should be assured to remain in the workforce or return when ready, with partnerships between Government, community and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Mothers need to feel at ease and assured to remain in the workforce and pursue their career aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: As for those who have taken or would need to take some time off to be a stay-home mom, they need to be confident that they can always return to the workforce when they feel ready to do so and feel welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: I could not agree more with Assoc Prof Razwana Begum that successful implementation of any initiatives will require cooperative partnerships between the Government, community and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: We cannot simply fall back on the assumption that this is all the Government's responsibility, and we all have a role to play in supporting families.

sections.label: Amendment on family policies motion
sections.summary: The Speaker puts to the House Mr Leong Man Wai's amendment to delete "continued review and updating" and insert "re-imagination" in the motion on family policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I shall put the question on the amendment to the House for a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have one amendment proposed by Mr Leong Man Wai.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The amendment is, "In Line 2, to delete the words "continued review and updating" and insert "re-imagination"".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That this House calls for the continued review and updating of policies to better support families, as well as the marriage and parenthood aspirations of Singaporeans, and endorses a whole-of-society approach to build a Singapore Made for Families." Those who agree, say "Aye".
